title: Otis and the Pidgeon's Perfect Coo
markdown:
Dawn painted the town pink and orange. Dewdrops glittered as if they had rehearsed. Otis the otter bounced from his nook, whiskers already employed. “Morning’s here!” His bright eyes found Mei the heron by the fountain. “Ready for a splendid day?”

Mei nodded. “A perfect morning for quiet observation.” She said it as if quiet were a picnic she had packed.

Maestro Quill bustled in, cello under his arm, spectacles adjusted with ceremony. “Today this square shall have truly serious music.” He pictured a concert hall. This was no day for giggles. He drew the bow. A powerful solemn note bloomed. Otis and Mei paused, captivated.

Then, from the clock tower, a soft coo.

Coo.

It landed perfectly on the end of the note. A curious beat, as if the tower had been waiting for a cue.

Maestro Quill frowned and played another sad note.

Coo.

Again, precision. Otis’s grin stretched. Mei tilted her head. “That’s Percy.”

The music swelled. Passion, poured.

COO.

Louder, punctuating the peak, a witty remark in pigeon. Giggles rippled through the early risers. Otis snorted. Mei chuckled, which for a heron is a dignified event.

Shoulders stiffened. A delicate passage.

Coo.

The coo arrived just as the bow paused, inventing a hilarious silence. The crowd roared.

Maestro Quill’s face went pink. He switched to a lively jig.

Coo-coo-COO.

Percy’s rhythm was impeccable, a counterpoint with feathers. He was, it appeared, the square’s comic expert, unpaid and punctual.

The square vibrated. Otis rolled on his back, kicking. Mei had tears of the useful kind. Maestro Quill, seeing the joy he had accidentally conducted, stopped. He looked at Percy, then at the laughing faces. A slow genuine smile arrived, late and honest.

He picked up the bow, winked at otter and heron, and began a new tune: still beautiful, now with a playful bounce. Percy added the coos on time, turning the morning into a duet the clock tower had been practising in secret.

Otis did not declare the day a marvel of the age. He logged solemn-note / Percy’s full stop / jig-with-coo in a damp pocket notebook, left a crumb on the fountain rim as a critic’s fee, and bounced out of the square already humming the pause. Mei resumed observation, which now included pigeons. Maestro Quill, cello still serious, had learned that a coo can be an instrument if you let it finish the bar.
